The '''2016–17 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Virginia]] during the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], in their 112th season of play. The team was led by head coach Tony Bennett, in his eighth year, and played their home games at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 23–11, 11–7 in ACC play to finish in [[2016–17 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for fifth place. They defeated [[2016–17 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] in the second round of the [[2017 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] to advance to the quarterfinals where they lost to [[2016–17 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 5 seed in the East region. There they defeated [[2016–17 UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball team|UNC Wilmington]] in the First Round before losing in the Second Round to [[2016–17 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]].

==Previous season==
Coming off of two highly successful regular seasons in [[2013–14 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2014]] and [[2014–15 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2015]], but with early exits from the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament all-time team records|NCAA tournament]] each time, and with the final season for seniors [[Malcolm Brogdon]] and [[Anthony Gill (basketball)|Anthony Gill]], expectations were high for the program in [[2015–16 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2015–16]]. However, the regular season was mixed: despite wins against programs like [[2015–16 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]], [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]], [[2015–16 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]], and [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], the team also suffered upsets to [[2015–16 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]], [[2015–16 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]], and [[2015–16 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. Despite this, the Cavaliers finished the season 29–8 overall and 13–5 in conference play, finishing at second place in the ACC. They fell in the [[2015 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] championship to [[2014–15 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite
